messages.subject: Count and ddply and arrays
parts:
> count(matrix(1:9,3,3))
  X1 X2 X3 freq
1  1  4  7    1
> count(matrix(rep(1,9),3,3))
  X1 X2 X3 freq
1  1  1  1    1

These don't seem like useful results. Count should either do something sensible or give an error for non-dataframes.

> count(floor(1:4/2))
  x freq
1 0    1
2 1    2
3 2    1

For a vector argument, count is actually useful -- but this case isn't mentioned in the documentation and isn't consistent with ddply's handling of vectors:

> ddply(floor(1:4/2),.(),print)
Error in rep(1, nrow(data)) : invalid 'times' argument

 And it is bizarre that count considers the elements of a vector to be in column "x":

> count(floor(1:4/2),"x")
  x freq
1 0    1
2 1    2
3 2    1

Actually, I think count should be done away with and replaced with a better way to refer to "all columns" in ddply.  More flexible and more orthogonal.

Similarly, ddply doesn't seem to check its argument type if it is an array:

> ddply(matrix(1:9,3,3,dimnames=list(c("a","b","c"),c("d","e","f"))),"d",sum)
Error in FUN(X[[1L]], ...) : numeric 'envir' arg not of length one

It might be sensible to convert it to data.frame (though there must be a more efficient way of grouping array rows by value?):

> ddply(as.data.frame(matrix(1:9,3,3,dimnames=list(c("a","b","c"),c("d","e","f")))),"d",sum)
  d V1
1 1 12
2 2 15
3 3 18

         -s
